document: FF-2 statement-fidelity signoff v0.1 (atom skin + pillowcase)
reviewer: independent fidelity reviewer subagent, Claude Opus, spawned by skeleton 2026-11-04
scope: Meaning review only: each of the 28 frozen statements read with the Lean definitions in force, against WORK_ORDER_v0_3.md. Compilation, kernel replay and axiom audit are not part of this review and were not performed. No Lean was run, no network was used, nothing was posted, no existing file was modified.
pin_crosscheck: Hash prefixes cited in FF2_FREEZE_DECISION_v0_1.md and REPAIR_DECISION_v0_1.md (8e108ff4, 61ca7137, b4484f6e, a1ea047d, b8a03b38, 3a525076) equal the files reviewed.

review_scripts.result: ALL OK: 28/28 delivered statements equal the frozen headers (whitespace-normalised) in the right namespace; no extra public declarations; 98 private helpers (29 Counts, 39 Pen, 30 Pillowcase); no sorry/axiom/instance/attribute/notation/variable/native_decide lines; AtomSkinData namespace block byte-equal to definitions v0.3; PillowcaseData namespace block byte-equal to definitions v0.1 (and v0.3).

2,153,901 checks, 0 failures. FINITE EVIDENCE, NOT PROOF: omega = 3..9 (every vertex, edge, square, state, sign); Part B on a, b = 1..6 over a +-3-period window, plus literal pairwise pillowRel search for a, b <= 3. Includes negative controls: dropping eps(v) from the boundary breaks A4 (omega 3..6); flipping the sign in pen_oriented_square fails in every state.
review_scripts.note: A first run reported 4536 failures in the two B2 HasFixingHalfTurn tags; cause was the reviewer's own search range for (i, j) being smaller than the point window (|X| up to 6a needs |i| up to 6). Range widened; recorded output is the corrected run. Not a defect in the Lean sources.

targets.name: vertex_count
targets.scope_note: card (Finset (Fin omega)) = 2^omega in N. Guard hω unused by the claim; harmless.

targets.name: edge_count
targets.scope_note: Edge = {(v,d) // d ∉ v}, one representative per cube edge (lower vertex, direction), as §3 'Edges'. omega*2^(omega-1) in N.

targets.name: square_count
targets.scope_note: Square = {(v,i) // i ∉ v ∧ next i ∉ v}, one representative per square. omega*2^(omega-2) in N.

targets.name: chi_formula
targets.scope_note: chi is V - E + F computed in Z from the three Fintype.card values, exactly the order's chi; rhs 2^(omega-2)*(4 - (omega:Z)) in Z, no N truncation.

targets.name: incident_pair_distinct
targets.scope_note: The two named squares at edge e (seat pairs {d-1,d} and {d,d+1}) are distinct. True already because their seat indices prev d and d differ (omega >= 3); that is the right reason, not a vacuous one.

targets.name: incident_pair_exhaustive
targets.scope_note: 'e is a face of f' is encoded as coefficient f e ≠ 0. Faithful because the four boundary edges of a square are distinct, so no cancellation (finite check: support = the 4 geometric face edges, omega 3..9). Squares named are squareAt (lower e) (prev d) and squareAt (lower e) d, i.e. seat pairs {d-1,d} and {d,d+1} as in the order.

targets.name: incident_square_count
targets.scope_note: 'exactly two squares', same face encoding as above.

targets.name: incident_direction_equiv
targets.scope_note: The incident edges at x biject with Fin omega by their direction; this identifies the link's vertex set ('edge directions at x') with the labels used in link_cycle.

targets.name: link_cycle
targets.scope_note: linkAdjacent x i j (i ≠ j and some square has x, x⊕i, x⊕j as corners, i.e. a square at x with directions {i,j}) iff j = i+1 or i = j+1 mod omega: the adjacency of C_omega on Fin omega. Together with incident_direction_equiv this is the order's 'link isomorphic to C_omega' as a simple graph. The relation form does not itself count edge multiplicity; multiplicity one follows from A2's count of exactly two squares per edge (informal combination), and the finite check confirms exactly one square per adjacent pair at every x (omega 3..9).

targets.name: incident_coefficients_opposite
targets.scope_note: Hypotheses f ≠ g and both coefficients nonzero are satisfiable (A2), so not vacuous. Holds because of the eps(v) factor: hand derivation gives -eps(v) from the {d-1,d} square and +eps(v) from the {d,d+1} square of edge (v,d); negative control without eps fails.

targets.name: total_boundary_zero
targets.scope_note: Sum over all squares of boundary = 0 in Chain1 = Edge →₀ Z, i.e. ∂(Σ squares) = 0 in C1.

targets.name: cube_edge_iff
targets.scope_note: Cube adjacency (differ by one toggle) iff the pair are the two ends of some Edge: the skin's 1-skeleton is the full omega-cube graph.

targets.name: cube_connected
targets.scope_note: Explicit path v : N → Vertex of length n with cube-adjacent steps between any x, y (n = 0 allowed for x = y). Uses cubeAdjacent, which cube_edge_iff ties to the Edge type.

targets.name: chi_even
targets.scope_note: Even in Z.

targets.name: genus_formula
targets.scope_note: genus = 1 - chi/2 in Z (Int division exact because chi is even); rhs 1 + ((omega:Z) - 4)*2^(omega-3) avoids the N-truncation the order warns about. Numerical invariant only, as the order's standing says.

targets.name: cube_genus_zero
targets.scope_note: Special case omega = 3 with the guard as a binder h3 : 3 ≤ 3; value 0, as the order states.

targets.name: pen_adjacent_seat
targets.scope_note: New direction d is next b or prev b (d ≡ b ± 1 mod omega) and d ≠ b; the second conjunct is redundant for omega ≥ 3 but harmless.

targets.name: pen_oriented_square
targets.scope_note: Exists a square f containing the back edge (w, b) and the new edge (w, d) (both coefficients nonzero), and the arriving move w⊕b → w and departing move w → w⊕d each have directed coefficient = signValue s × their coefficient in ∂f: s = +1 runs along ∂f, s = -1 against it. directedCoefficient is never 0 for these moves (checked), so the equations are substantive; negative control with the opposite sign fails in every state (omega 3..9). The square is unique (checked). 'Oriented boundary' means the order's ∂ with the eps(v) factor.

targets.name: pen_return_four
targets.scope_note: Full state (vertex and back direction) returns at iterate 4, for every state and fixed s.

targets.name: pen_no_earlier_return
targets.scope_note: Not at k = 1, 2, 3 (0 < k < 4); hypotheses exactly the needed range.

targets.name: pen_four_corners
targets.scope_note: The image of iterates 0..3 on vertices equals corners f as a Finset; since corners has 4 elements, the four visited vertices are distinct and are the corners of one square.

targets.name: pillowRel_equivalence
targets.scope_note: pillowRel is exactly the order's relation (w = v + (2ia,2jb) or w = -v + (2ia,2jb)). Guards 0 < a, 0 < b are the order's binders; the claim would also hold without them (harmless).

targets.name: key_classifies
targets.scope_note: key(v) = key(w) iff v ~ w for all integer points, with net/key transcribing the order's recipe step for step. The optional group-orbit reading was not formalised, so B1 is for the arithmetic relation, which the order permits. No viewer-string bridge claimed. Finite check: class count 2ab + 2 for every a, b ≤ 6.

targets.name: halfTurn_not_identity
targets.scope_note: Every half-turn (including the one about (0,0)) moves some point, so it is a non-identity map; holds for all a, b without guards. A weak sanity statement by design; it supports B2's 'non-identity stabilizer' reading.

targets.name: fixingHalfTurn_iff_multiples
targets.scope_note: Supporting statement not listed by name in the order: a half-turn fixes v iff v = (ia, jb), i.e. v is a half-turn centre. Guards unneeded but harmless.

targets.name: nonzero_translation_fixes_nothing
targets.scope_note: i ≠ 0 or j ≠ 0 means the translation vector (2ia, 2jb) ≠ 0 under the guards; the guards are needed here (a = 0 would make i ≠ 0 the identity).

targets.name: fixingHalfTurn_iff_corner_class
targets.scope_note: HasFixingHalfTurn is the order's own operational meaning of 'non-identity stabilizer' ('some half-turn fixes it'); with nonzero_translation_fixes_nothing and halfTurn_not_identity it covers every element of the form the relation uses. No group or stabilizer object is defined (the group reading was optional), so the stabilizer wording is carried by this decomposition, not by a formal stabilizer.

targets.name: four_corner_classes_distinct
targets.scope_note: corner c ~ corner d iff c = d over Bool × Bool, the four classes of (0,0), (a,0), (0,b), (a,b): pairwise distinct.

definitions.name: Vertex
definitions.note: Finset (Fin omega).

definitions.name: Edge
definitions.note: {(v,d) // d ∉ v}: edge {v, v ∪ {d}}, one representative.

definitions.name: cyclicDir / next / prev
definitions.note: Fin.ofNat omega ((z % omega).toNat); Int % is Euclidean so the residue is in [0, omega). next = i+1, prev = i-1 mod omega: the declared cyclic order as data.

definitions.name: Square
definitions.note: {(v,i) // i ∉ v ∧ next i ∉ v}.

definitions.name: mkEdge / lower / upper / toggle
definitions.note: mkEdge v d normalises to (v \ {d}, d), so it names the edge in direction d at v whether or not d ∈ v. toggle = symmetric difference with {d}.

definitions.name: squareAt / corners
definitions.note: squareAt x i = ((x \ {i}) \ {i+1}, i): the square with seat pair {i, i+1} through x. corners = {v, v∪i, v∪j, v∪{i,j}}.

definitions.name: Chain1
definitions.note: Edge →₀ Z is C1. C0 and C2 are not defined as types; C2 appears only as the sum over squares in total_boundary_zero, and no target needs C0. Harmless omission.

definitions.name: boundary
definitions.note: eps(v)·(e(v,i) + e(v∪i, j) - e(v∪j, i) - e(v, j)), j = next i, term for term as in §3. It is a genuine 1-cycle (∂1∂2 = 0, finite check) and the eps factor is load-bearing for A4 (control). Repair consequence: noncomputable (Finsupp subtraction), so boundary cannot be #eval-ed as a certificate; the propositions are unchanged.

definitions.name: coefficient
definitions.note: boundary f e. Noncomputable for the same reason; no #eval certificate.

definitions.name: edgeIncident / cubeAdjacent
definitions.note: Endpoint incidence; one-toggle adjacency.

definitions.name: linkAdjacent
definitions.note: Adjacency of i ≠ j iff some square at x has x⊕i, x⊕j as corners, which forces {i,j} to be that square's seat pair: the order's link edges. Relation form (simple graph); see link_cycle note.

definitions.name: chi / genus
definitions.note: chi in Z from cards; genus = 1 - chi/2 in Z (Int division exact since chi is even).

definitions.name: Sign / signValue
definitions.note: Two constructors, ±1. Repair dropped Fintype from deriving; no statement needs it.

definitions.name: State / step
definitions.note: State = (w, b). step = (toggle w d, d) with d = cyclicDir(b - signValue s · eps(w)), the order's d = b - s·ε(w) mod omega. The order cites template line 153; the template is outside this review's closed file list, so step was checked against the order's transcription only.

definitions.name: directedCoefficient
definitions.note: +1 for lower→upper traversal, -1 for upper→lower, 0 otherwise. Used only in pen_oriented_square, where it is never 0.

definitions.name: Point / translation / halfTurn / pillowRel
definitions.note: ℤ × ℤ; v + (2ia, 2jb); (2ia, 2jb) - v, the half-turn about (ia, jb); the order's relation verbatim.

definitions.name: net
definitions.note: x = X mod 2a, y = Y mod 2b; if y > b then (((2a - x) mod 2a), 2b - y). N subtraction is safe because x < 2a, y < 2b when a, b > 0. Unguarded definition: meaningless for a = 0 or b = 0, but every theorem carries 0 < a, 0 < b.

definitions.name: PillowKey / key
definitions.note: Constructors boundary/front/back (r y : N); r = x if x ≤ a else 2a - x; boundary if r ∈ {0, a} or y ∈ {0, b}, else front if x < a, else back: the order's recipe.

definitions.name: HasFixingHalfTurn
definitions.note: ∃ i j, halfTurn i j v = v: 'some half-turn fixes it'.

definitions.name: corner
definitions.note: (0,0), (a,0), (0,b), (a,b) indexed by Bool × Bool.

private_helpers.finding: All are declared private; the only public declarations in the three proof modules are the 28 frozen theorems. No instance, attribute, notation, variable, set_option, axiom, sorry or native_decide lines in any of the five sources, so no helper adds a public claim or changes elaboration of the public statements. Helpers duplicated across Counts and Pen are private in separate modules (Pen does not import Counts).

other_observations: The two Data sources keep the definition file's header comment ('Proposed exact definition bytes, not an executable proof file ... No target proof is present') outside the namespace. Cosmetic; the binding rule compares the namespace block, which is byte-equal.
The order's optional items (injective prime labelling / divisor reading, group-orbit reading of the relation, viewer-string bridge) are not formalised and not claimed. Part C is out of scope.
The atom skin pen template v0.2 is outside the closed file list; 'computed as in the template' was checked against the work order's prose only.
overall_result: PASS (meaning review): all 28 statements and all reviewed definitions say what WORK_ORDER_v0_3.md Parts A and B ask for, within the order's own standing (exact combinatorial certificate and numerical invariant; lattice-point statements; no surface, orbifold or covering theorem). This signoff is independent of and does not substitute for the recompile, kernel replay and axiom audit.
